meta.title: The Greenmarch
meta.author: DungeonMaster
meta.description: A worked example of a complete game flow: biome to area to point of interest, gated progression, encounters with odds, loot limited by what a character has become, a staged quest with dialogue and memory, and creatures that react to each other rather than only to the party.

senses.name: Sight
senses.description: What you can see, which is nothing at all through a wall. Either something is in view or it is not, so every threshold is the same.

senses.name: Hearing
senses.description: Sound travels in a straight line and stops at stone, but passes reeds and open doorways perfectly well. It fades with distance, so a far-off clatter is worth walking towards and a near one is worth drawing steel for.

senses.name: Smell
senses.description: Scent seeps around corners and hangs about long after you have gone. A hound follows where you went rather than where you are, and a cold trail is faint even underfoot.

stances.name: Sneak
stances.description: Slow and careful. Half pace, a fifth the noise, and rather less of your smell on the wind.

stances.name: Walk
stances.description: An ordinary pace. Nothing gained, nothing given away.

stances.name: Dash
stances.description: Quick, and heard from a long way off.

opportunities.name: Parting Blow
opportunities.description: Anyone who walks out of your reach gives you one free swing, which is what makes disengaging a decision rather than a formality.

skills.name: Stealth
skills.description: Moving without being heard. Ranks quieten a careful step further; nothing makes you silent outright.

items.name: Brass Key
items.description: Worn smooth. It opens the mill.

requires.description: Only a reader of runes recognises it as more than a rock.
The barrow only yields its blade to a proven party.

reactions.description: A hound that watches a packmate die goes berserk — creatures act on each other, not only on the party.
Last one standing, badly hurt: it tests its nerve and may break.
It knows who robbed the barrow, and goes for them first.

npcs.name: Vess the Miller
npcs.description: Ran the mill until something moved into it.

reactions.description: If she has heard you steal, she stops dealing with you — memory changing behaviour, not just dialogue.

terrains.name: Shallow Water
terrains.description: Ankle deep and slow going, but you can wade it.

triggers.description: Ambient colour, every visit, never remembered.

areas.name: Millford
areas.description: A handful of roofs where the road meets the water.

areas.name: The Fens
areas.description: Standing water and older things under it.

triggers.description: Fires once, and is remembered — the world keeps a record that you have been here.
Repeats until the mill is actually clear, then stops for good.
Leave it unfinished and the barrow reorders itself — the restart mode.

gates.name: The Mill Door
gates.description: Barred from the inside. The brass key opens it; a good hand with picks can manage without.

gates.name: The Barrow Ward
gates.description: A carved seal. It answers to spoken runes, or to someone the Wardens vouch for.

requires.description: Only stalks parties that have made a name.

variants.text: Something moves out there, {direction} of you, and does not care who knows it.
A heavy splash, {direction}. Then nothing.
Reeds crack somewhere {direction}.
A sound, maybe. Somewhere {direction}.
You stop. Whatever it was does not come again.
Far off {direction}, something disturbs the water.
Wet fur and old meat, carried {direction} on the air.
A rank animal smell, close enough to place: {direction}.
Something has been through here recently, and it stank.
The wind turns and brings something sour off the {direction} water.
A trace of musk in the reeds, going cold.
Something passed this way. Hours ago, by the smell.
Millford, such as it is: six roofs, a wet road, and the wheel standing still.
Smoke sits low over Millford. Nobody is on the road.
The village holds its breath. The mill wheel has not turned in weeks.
The ground stops being ground. Water lies in sheets between the alders.
The fens open out, flat and brown and patient.
Reeds close over the path. Something moves, far off, and stops when you stop.
Mist comes off the water in slow ropes.
Something calls once, across the water, and is not answered.
The smell of iron and rot rises where you step.
Dressed stone, laid dry, still true after all this time.
The passage narrows. Carvings run along the lintel, worn past reading.
Cold air moves against your face from somewhere ahead.
The door does not give. Something heavy is set against it on the inside.
Barred. You can hear the beam shift when you push.
It holds. Whatever is in there wants to stay in there.
The hound sees its packmate fall and comes apart with rage.
A shriek goes up, and the survivor stops being careful.
It abandons the circling and simply comes at you.
The water goes still. Something is standing in it that was not.
A grey shape resolves out of the mist, unhurried.
The cold arrives before it does.
You hold still. Water, reeds, your own breathing. Nothing else.
Nothing but the fen shifting about, and none of it in a hurry.
You listen a while. Whatever is out there is not moving.
Wet peat and rot, and under it nothing that has passed lately.
The air is all bog. Nothing has come this way.
You take the air. Old water, and no trail in it.
Mud, thatch, and the smell of the fen. The mill stands at the end of the road with its wheel dead still.
A dozen houses leaning on one another. Somebody is watching from a doorway and not coming out.
The road gives up here at the water. The mill is the only building worth the name, and nothing moves in it.
Vess wants the mill back. Whatever is in it does not agree.
The miller's problem is now your problem.
Clear the mill. Simple enough, said in a warm room.

says.text: "You'll be the ones the Wardens sent. Good. I want my mill back."
"Sit if you like. I'd offer better, but everything I own is in that mill."
"You came. I'd half stopped expecting anyone."

options.text: It's done. The mill is clear.
It'll cost you more than thanks.

options.lockedHint: She doesn't know you well enough to open the chest.

says.text: "Wheel stopped. I went to see why. I did not go in."
"Something took it in the wet season. I heard it before I saw the door barred."
"You want the truth? I ran. I'm not ashamed of it."
"Then take the key. Brass one. Don't lose it — there isn't another."
"Here. It sticks. Lean on it."
"The key, and my thanks, and that's all I have."
"...Fine. Fine. There's coin under the floor. It's yours when it's done."
She looks at you a long moment. "You drive a hard bargain for a wet village."
"Take it, then. I'd rather be poor and sleeping."
"I've nothing to give that I haven't offered. Take it or don't."
"You can see what I have. It's all in that mill."
She doesn't answer. That is an answer.
"Then I'll sleep tonight. That's worth more than the coin."
"You have my thanks, and the Wardens will hear of it."
She sits down slowly, as if she had been standing for weeks.
"I've heard what you are. Get off my step."
She does not open the door all the way. "No. Not you."
"Word travels, even out here. Go on."

quests.name: Wet Boots
quests.description: The Wardens sent you down to Millford because someone here asked for help and nobody else would come.

objectives.description: Find Vess the miller and hear what she wants.

requires.description: Offered once the Wardens are not actively suspicious.

stages.name: Get inside
stages.description: The door is barred. The key or the picks.

quests.name: The Barrow Ward
quests.description: There is older trouble under the fens, and the mill was only its edge.

requires.description: Only once the mill is done and the party can survive it.

objectives.description: Find what the fens are hiding.

rules.name: Vess never forgets a theft
rules.description: The GM pins this one: whatever the simulation decides, Vess learns of a theft and never lets it go.

rules.name: The barrow keeps its own counsel
rules.description: Nothing living saw it, so opening the barrow spreads only to the things of the fen.
